newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia Lippo restructuring plan hits problem.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia Lippo restructuring plan hits problem.

text.p: Indonesia's stock market supervisory agency Bapepam said on Friday it was against conglomerate Lippo Group's plan to restructure its finance division through cross-holdings.
The agency's controlling department head Herwidayatmo told Reuters that in principle, Bapepam would not allow the cross or mutual holding practice in Indonesia.
Herwidayatmo said if planned restructurings among group subsidiaries Lippo Securities, Lippo Life and Lippo Bank were completed, there will be mutual or cross-holdings within the Lippo Group.
On August 28, Lippo Securities said it planned to buy a 26.99 percent stake in Lippo Life. Lippo Life then planned to buy 40.15 percent of the shares in Lippo Bank.
But Herwidayatmo noted Lippo Bank already held a 11.67 percent stake in Lippo Life. Also Lippo Life has an indirect 9.46 percent stake in Lippo Securities.
Herwidayatmo said the agency had sent a letter to Lippo Securities, Lippo Life and Lippo Bank with two main questions.
"First, what is the benefit of the restructuring for investors. Second, are they willing to continue the restructuring plan after omitting the cross-holding," he said.
Besides, Lippo Life, the group's insurance unit, should get written approval from Director General of Financial Institution on its plan to increase its stake in PT Lippo Bank, he added.
A source at the Lippo Group told Bisnis Indonesia newspaper that the plan has now been put on hold.
"We will soon make our report and submit it to Bapepam," the source was quoted as saying.
